raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Three fixes around KV cache allocation for local-attention models and spec-decode
drafters. Found via Laguna-S-2.1 + DFlash, but only one commit is model-specific.
On current main (GB10, Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4, DFlash, fp8 KV, max_model_len
131072, max_num_seqs 16, 23.1 GB KV pool) the series takes the KV pool from
415,517 to 871,430 tokens (2.1x), with draft acceptance unchanged.

1. Drafter layers of EAGLE-family speculators get scattered across KV cache
   groups by the strided group assignment in
   `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size`. Fix: identify drafter layers
   (index >= target layer count, gated on `use_eagle()`) and give dedicated
   groups to the specs whose drafter layers would otherwise share a group with
   target layers. Sharing corrupts the drafter's absolute-slot context writes,
   which resolve through the target's block table: on Laguna-S-2.1 draft
   acceptance falls to 0.29% versus 26.67% with a dedicated group, at an
   identical pool size. On the V1 model runner the same layout instead trips
   the assertion in `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.validate_same_kv_cache_group` at
   startup. Separation is conditional because regrouping changes the
   group-size heuristic's inputs: separating regardless cut Qwen3.5-9B's pool
   from 863k to 185k tokens. Works for any PP size; the strided layout still
   applies to target layers.
2. `laguna_dflash.py` cleared the drafter's `attn.sliding_window`, forcing
   FullAttentionSpec on all 6 drafter layers (measured 38% of the pool for KV
   outside the window the drafter never reads). The `DFlashQwen3Model` base
   class already supports windowed draft layers; the clearing appears to be a
   workaround for the group-sharing corruption fixed in commit 1. Qwen3.5 DFlash
   avoids that corruption because its per-layer specs already give one group
   per layer, so its drafter never shares. Fix: keep the checkpoint-declared
   window.
3. `SlidingWindowSpec` and `ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec` charge the global
   `max_in_flight_tokens` bound to every request when sizing the pool. Since
   `sum_r (window - 1 + in_flight_r) <= R*(window - 1) + max_in_flight_tokens`,
   per-request sizing only needs the request's share of the allowance. Fix:
   amortize over `max_num_seqs`; the runtime admission gate is unchanged, and
   sizing is identical to today at `max_num_seqs = 1`. Without this, fixes 1
   and 2 barely show (347k to 352k tokens), because sliding layers are charged
   almost like full attention.

## Scope

- Commit 1: any EAGLE-family drafter (eagle/eagle3/mtp/dflash/dspark) over a
  hybrid target. All in-tree EAGLE-family implementations register drafter
  layers with indices continuing after the target's
  (`start_layer_id=target_layer_num` / `mtp_start_layer_idx=num_hidden_layers`),
  so identification cannot misclassify a target layer; unparseable names are
  skipped. No speculative config means grouping is unchanged.
- Commit 2: Laguna only. Removes a divergence from its own base class.
- Commit 3: every model using SlidingWindowSpec (Gemma 2/3/4, gpt-oss,
  Command R, EXAONE 4, and others), SlidingWindowMLASpec by inheritance, and
  ChunkedLocalAttentionSpec (Llama 4 style local attention). Broadest behavior
  change of the three; can be split into its own PR if preferred. The chunked
  local part is unit-tested only (no such model available for E2E here).

## Not duplicating existing PRs

- #35062: same root cause as commit 1 (referenced in the commit message),
  stalled on rebase since June. Differences: per-spec drafter groups (a single
  merged group would mix specs for hybrid drafters), identification gated to
  `use_eagle()` (independent `draft_model` drafters number from 0), rebased
  with tests. Happy to defer to a revived #35062; will comment there.
- #46032: relaxes the same-group invariant for `DraftModelProposer` only.
  EAGLE-family proposers still assert a single group. Complementary.
- Nothing open covers commits 2 or 3.

## Test plan and results

- `pytest tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_swa_inflight_window_free.py
  tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/test_kv_cache_spec_registry.py`:
  131 passed, 0 failed (needs a GPU; some device-inference tests fail in a
  GPU-less container with or without this change). New tests:
  `test_drafter_layers_get_dedicated_kv_cache_group`,
  `test_drafter_layer_identification_requires_eagle_family`,
  `test_sliding_window_pool_sizing_amortizes_in_flight_tokens`,
  `test_chunked_local_pool_sizing_amortizes_in_flight_tokens`. Two existing
  tests that hardcoded the old sizing constants now pin `max_num_seqs=1`, where
  old and new sizing coincide.
- Validated on a second real model, not simulated:
  `Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound` with `z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash` at 30b0d54
  (hybrid drafter, 5 sliding + 1 full; auto-selects the V2 runner). Pool
  863,023 stock vs 864,749 with this PR, and identical spec-decode counters,
  i.e. exactly neutral. Synthetic `KVCacheSpec` fixtures were not predictive
  here, indicating no change for a configuration that in fact lost 79% of the
  pool, so grouping claims are traced inside the live engine.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files.
- Test env: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.26.1rc1.dev18+gd223c900d), branch
  rebased onto that exact commit, changed files mounted over the installed
  package (aarch64 box, no source install). Should be re-run in a source install
  before merge.

E2E on GB10, Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4 + DFlash, fp8 KV, `max_model_len` 131072,
`max_num_seqs` 16, 23.1 GB KV pool, V2 runner:

| | pool tokens | max conc @128k |
|---|---|---|
| stock main | 415,517 | 3.17x |
| + commits 1-2 | 466,211 | 3.56x |
| + commit 3 | 871,430 | 6.65x |

Acceptance, paired (identical seeded prompts in both arms, 15 speculative
tokens):

| context | stock | this PR | paired diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ~59 tokens (below the 512 window, no eviction) | 15.20% | 16.73% | +1.53pp (t=1.12) |
| ~7,050 tokens (well above the window) | 17.82% | 23.48% | +5.65pp (t=0.84) |

Both favour this PR and neither is significant, so I read this as no acceptance
regression. Power caveat: the long-context paired sd is 13.5pp, so that row
shows no evidence of a cost rather than proving neutrality. An earlier unpaired
comparison suggested a ~2.8pp deficit; it did not survive pairing, because
between-boot and between-prompt variance dominate on this checkpoint (greedy is
non-deterministic from atomic-add reductions). Coherence (greedy known-answer)
passes on every configuration. A controlled prefill/decode throughput A/B for
commit 3 alone (on the prior 0.25 nightly, same box) showed no change and zero
preemptions; throughput on this image was only sanity-checked.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code) was used to investigate, draft,
and test this change. The submitter has reviewed every line and re-run the
tests.

_Edited: corrected the separation criterion to sharing-only after it was
found to cost capacity, and replaced simulated and mismatched-length
measurements with paired real-model ones._

I found a Qwen3.5 DFlash correctness case that appears to challenge the
assumption in commit 2 that SlidingWindowSpec is safe for DFlash draft layers.

Test setup:
- vLLM CPU v0.26.0, V2 model runner
- Target: Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound
- Draft: z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash retrain, revision
  30b0d54fe1e8aa5543387cc131503b2afe2f6a9c
- Draft layout: 5 sliding-attention layers and 1 full-attention layer
- 15 speculative tokens

Results:
| Configuration | Acceptance rate | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original SlidingWindowSpec allocation | 2.29% | 1.34 |
| All-full-attention control | 33.03% | 5.95 |
| Hybrid compute with full KV allocation for SWA layers | 33.03% | 5.95 |
| Same fix without the causal=false override | 33.03% | 5.95 |

Setting the configured window to 262144, using only one sliding layer, and
using all sliding layers did not recover acceptance. The only change that
recovered it was retaining the layer's sliding-window compute configuration
while setting the inner Attention.sliding_window to None for KV-cache planning.

Qwen3 DFlash precomputes verifier-context K/V and writes it through absolute
context slot mappings. SlidingWindowManager's normal autoregressive block
recycling appears to invalidate that context.

I have a small Qwen3 patch matching Laguna's existing full-allocation behavior,
plus a focused regression test. Would you prefer this correctness case to be
handled in #50169 or in a separate PR? It may also be worth validating Laguna
acceptance quality, rather than coherence alone, before removing its safeguard.

Disclosure: GHC assisted the code/history investigation and patch
drafting. I reviewed the changes and ran the reported experiments.

Thanks for this, it found a real bug in the PR. You were right that the safety
argument in commit 2 was not established, and I have pushed a fix.

What I reproduced, on GB10 (CUDA), Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4 + DFlash, V2 model runner,
15 speculative tokens, everything else held constant:

| Laguna config | draft acceptance | KV pool |
|---|---:|---:|
| windowed drafter, stock grouping | 0.29% (n=4, sd 0.08) | 871,430 |
| windowed drafter, drafter in its own KV group | 26.67% (n=2) | 871,430 |

Same pool either way, so this is not an allocation-size effect. The collapse
matches what you measured, and my earlier Laguna runs missed it because they
always had the grouping commit applied.

The root cause looks narrower than "SlidingWindowSpec is unsafe for DFlash". It
is a drafter layer sharing a KV cache group with target layers: the absolute
context slot mapping then resolves through the target's block table. Drafter
layers that have their groups to themselves are fine windowed. So the PR now
separates a drafter spec only when it would otherwise share a group, and the
window can stay.

On your model I could not reproduce the collapse on GPU. Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound
with z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash at 30b0d54, V2 runner, 15 spec tokens:

| Qwen3.5 config | draft acceptance | KV pool |
|---|---:|---:|
| stock (windowed drafter) | 23.46% (n=5, sd 0.00) | 863,023 |
| full-attention drafter allocation | see note | 599,543 |
| this PR | 23.46% (n=5, sd 0.00) | 864,749 |

That model gives one KV group per layer, so its drafter never shares a group,
which is consistent with windowed being fine there. Stock and this PR produce
byte-identical spec-decode counters (accepted=813, drafted=3465 in every rep),
so the PR is exactly neutral on that model. The full-attention row is a
pool-only comparison; its acceptance was measured at a different generation
length and I have not re-run it like-for-like. Note that full allocation costs
31% of the pool there, which is why I would rather not apply it
unconditionally. Since your run was vLLM CPU v0.26.0, would you check whether
the CPU attention backend is the differentiating factor?

Your suggestion also caught a second bug. My first attempt separated the drafter
whenever its layers spanned several groups, which on Qwen3.5 merged five
single-layer groups into one five-layer group, violated the equal-layers-per-group
assumption in _get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size, and cut its pool from 863k
to 185k. The pushed version keys on sharing rather than spanning, and I added a
regression test for the untouched case.

Happy to take the Qwen3 patch here if you still want the belt-and-braces
behaviour after the CPU/GPU question is settled, or to review it separately.



_Edited: replaced the Qwen3.5 acceptance figures, which had been taken at mismatched generation lengths, with like-for-like measurements._

Thanks for reproducing this and for updating the grouping logic. I’ll test stock current main on the same Xeon CPU with the original hybrid Qwen3.5 layout, then compare #50169 and full allocation on the same build if the collapse remains.

The prior CPU controls may be relevant: one sliding layer, all six sliding layers in one draft group, and a 262144-token window all remained near 2.3% acceptance. I’ll report the current-main version, KV grouping/pool logs, and like-for-like acceptance counters.

Follow-up: I tested the retrained Qwen3.5 DFlash checkpoint on a CPU nightly:

- vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev124+gb88916617`
- commit: `b88916617d3d2249bff0dae5cecb6b727c980a20`
- target: `Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound`
- draft: retrained hybrid layout, 5 sliding-attention layers + 1 full-attention layer
- `num_speculative_tokens=15`
- Model Runner V2 with `triton-cpu@270e696d`
- eager mode, prefix caching disabled
- no `dflash_config.causal` override
- no local patch and no changes from this PR

Result:

- Acceptance rate: **32.61%**
- Acceptance length: **5.89**

For comparison, on v0.26.0 CPU:

- stock hybrid allocation: about **2.29% / 1.34**
- forcing full KV allocation for draft sliding layers: **33.03% / 5.95**

So current stock CPU nightly has healthy acceptance while retaining the checkpoint-declared sliding-window allocation. The recovery is already present before this PR; I have not isolated the exact intervening commit.

**Commit 3 can relax the startup feasibility gate below what runtime admission requires (hybrid MLA + sliding-window, large `max_model_len`)**

Thanks for this series — we carry commit 3 (`f401599bb`) downstream because without it our
config cannot start at all. Reporting a correctness concern about that commit specifically.

**Symptom.** The engine starts, logs a max-concurrency above 1.0 for `max_model_len`, and then
never schedules a single request of that size. The request sits in the waiting queue
indefinitely: `num_requests_waiting=1`, `num_requests_running=0`,
`iteration_tokens_total` stays at 0, `kv_cache_usage_perc` stays at 0. Cancelling the client
clears the queue and the server stays healthy. This is the #39734 deadlock shape.

**Why commit 3 is implicated.** `max_memory_usage_bytes` feeds
`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` ("can we serve at least one request at `max_model_len`") and
`get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` (the logged concurrency). Commit 3 divides the
in-flight term by `max_num_seqs` there. The runtime path is unchanged and still charges the
full allowance: `allocate_slots(..., full_sequence_must_fit=scheduler_reserve_full_isl)`
(default `True`) computes the whole sequence via `get_num_blocks_to_allocate(...,
apply_admission_cap=True)` and compares against actual free blocks. So the startup gate can
pass at a pool the runtime gate will always reject.

**Config** (identical across all rows): vLLM v0.27.1 with only commit 3 applied;
DeepSeek-V4-Pro (MLA + two sliding-window sizes) + DSpark speculative decoding
(`num_speculative_tokens=7`); DP4 x EP4, prefill on 4x B300 (267.69 GiB each);
`max_model_len=1048576`, `max_num_seqs=64`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`,
`block_size=256`, fp8 KV, chunked prefill and prefix caching on, async scheduling on.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | prefill KV pool | single 1,000,000-token request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.94 | 9.60 GiB / 7,176 blocks | never scheduled (>12 min, zero iteration tokens) |
| 0.955 | 13.61 GiB / 10,179 blocks | never scheduled |
| 0.96 | 14.55 GiB / 10,880 blocks (DP0), 11,180 (DP1-3) | admitted, HTTP 200 in 176-187 s |

At 0.94 the startup log reads:

```text
GPU KV cache size: 1,780,544 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 1,048,576 tokens per request: 1.70x
```

Back-solving that line (`num_blocks / concurrency`) gives **4,226 blocks per `max_model_len`
request**, while the runtime gate demands **10,180-10,880 blocks** for a slightly smaller
(1,000,000-token) request — a **2.4-2.6x under-estimate**. The engine advertises 1.70x
concurrency for a request size it cannot admit even once.

A coarse bisect at 0.94 (7,176 blocks) puts the largest schedulable prompt between 300,000
and 400,000 tokens: 300k completes in 35 s, 400k is never scheduled.

**Supporting datapoint for the direction of the error.** Without commit 3, on the same model
and `max_model_len`, `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` demands 15.36 GiB and refuses to start
at 0.95 (12.27 GiB available). That is above the 13.6-14.55 GiB the runtime actually needs,
i.e. the un-amortized gate errs conservatively. The amortized gate crosses below it.

**We tested commit 1 (`ecb28b3fa`) on this config; it does not address this.** Rebased onto
v0.27.1 (4 of 5 hunks apply; the `same_type_layers` hunk needs a manual rebase because v0.27.1
inserts a "further merge same-type layers" step after that loop). Applicability checks passed
before running: `use_eagle()` covers `dspark`, and this model's DSpark drafter registers its
attention layers as `layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}`, so `_identify_drafter_layers` finds them.
With the commit applied, the startup accounting is unchanged — `Maximum concurrency` stays at
2.57x/2.65x and the DP0 pool at 10,873 vs 10,860 blocks — and the runtime behaviour is
unchanged too. The conditional separation appears not to trigger here, i.e. our drafter layers
already have their groups to themselves. No regression from it either.

**Operational consequence.** Because the gate passes, the operator ends up choosing
utilization from the wrong number, and the remaining device headroom has to absorb both
CUDA graph capture and execution scratch. With CUDA graphs enabled at the utilization that
admits 1M, graph capture takes 3.94 GiB/device and prefill then dies mid-request with
`torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 976.00 MiB ... 857-869 MiB is free`, killing the
engine core. Reproduced twice, with and without commit 1. Our current workaround is asymmetric:
CUDA graphs on the decode instance only, prefill forced eager. That restores throughput
(decode-side ITL P95 71 ms -> 15 ms on an internal agent benchmark) while keeping 1M
schedulable, but it is a workaround for the accounting gap, not a fix.

**Suggested direction.** If the amortized value is the right one for aggregate pool-capacity
planning, it may still be worth having `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` — and ideally the
logged `Maximum concurrency` — use the same per-request bound the runtime admission gate uses
(`max_admission_blocks_per_request` with the full `max_in_flight_tokens`), so that "can one
`max_model_len` request fit" and "will the scheduler admit it" cannot disagree.

**What we did not establish.** We did not isolate which KV cache group's accounting produces
the 2.4x gap — only the aggregate. We have not written or tested a patch for the gap itself.
Happy to run any candidate on this config.

A data point relevant to commit 2 (keeping the drafter's checkpoint-declared window). It comes from a different model, but it is the same mechanism you'd get with a windowed Laguna drafter.

In #60560 we root-caused a DFlash2 acceptance drop (~40% → 27–29% at 32 concurrent sessions) that occurs only when the drafter's layers form a real sliding-window KV cache group. When `SlidingWindowManager` frees a block, the worker's block table keeps the old id. FA4 loads KV in 128-key tiles on SM100, so with 64-token pages the tile holding the window start can include one page that lies wholly outside the window. Once that freed block is reused, its bytes can decode as fp8 NaN, and masked NaN still reaches the attention output.

Two conditions hide it, so the GB10 checks here may not show it:
- **Low concurrency.** It nearly vanishes at concurrency 1 (37.9%), because freed blocks are rarely reused in time.
- **Tile size.** It needs the attention kernel's KV tile to be larger than the KV page. FA4 picks 64-key tiles on SM12x (for head dim > 64), so 64-token pages are safe there, while SM100 uses 128-key tiles.

It's worth re-checking Laguna acceptance on an SM100 GPU under sustained concurrency before relying on the windowed drafter. The fix, #60767 (nulling freed sliding-window entries in the worker's forward-pass block tables), would cover this PR's case too.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on all changed files.
- Test env: `vllm/vllm-openai:nightly` (0.26.1rc1.dev18+gd223c900d), branch
  rebased onto that exact commit, changed files mounted over the installed
  package (aarch64 box, no source install). Should be re-run in a source install
  before merge.

E2E on GB10, Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4 + DFlash, fp8 KV, `max_model_len` 131072,
`max_num_seqs` 16, 23.1 GB KV pool, V2 runner:

| | pool tokens | max conc @128k |
|---|---|---|
| stock main | 415,517 | 3.17x |
| + commits 1-2 | 466,211 | 3.56x |
| + commit 3 | 871,430 | 6.65x |

Acceptance, paired (identical seeded prompts in both arms, 15 speculative
tokens):

| context | stock | this PR | paired diff |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ~59 tokens (below the 512 window, no eviction) | 15.20% | 16.73% | +1.53pp (t=1.12) |
| ~7,050 tokens (well above the window) | 17.82% | 23.48% | +5.65pp (t=0.84) |

Both favour this PR and neither is significant, so I read this as no acceptance
regression. Power caveat: the long-context paired sd is 13.5pp, so that row
shows no evidence of a cost rather than proving neutrality. An earlier unpaired
comparison suggested a ~2.8pp deficit; it did not survive pairing, because
between-boot and between-prompt variance dominate on this checkpoint (greedy is
non-deterministic from atomic-add reductions). Coherence (greedy known-answer)
passes on every configuration. A controlled prefill/decode throughput A/B for
commit 3 alone (on the prior 0.25 nightly, same box) showed no change and zero
preemptions; throughput on this image was only sanity-checked.

## Disclosure

AI assistance (Claude Opus 5 via Claude Code) was used to investigate, draft,
and test this change. The submitter has reviewed every line and re-run the
tests.

_Edited: corrected the separation criterion to sharing-only after it was
found to cost capacity, and replaced simulated and mismatched-length
measurements with paired real-model ones._

+def test_drafter_layers_get_dedicated_kv_cache_group():
+    """EAGLE-family drafter layers must all land in one KV cache group.
+
+    `SpecDecodeBaseProposer.validate_same_kv_cache_group` requires all draft
+    layers in a single group, but the strided group assignment in
+    `_get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size` scatters the drafter's layers

+    sliding target layers + 6 DFlash drafter sliding layers -> the 42 sliding
+    layers form 4 strided groups with the drafter's 6 in all four). Drafter
+    layers are identified by layer index (EAGLE-family drafters continue the
+    target's numbering) and separated into a dedicated group, independent of
+    pipeline parallelism.

+def test_drafter_layers_alone_in_groups_are_left_untouched():

+def test_sliding_window_pool_sizing_amortizes_in_flight_tokens():
+    """Pool sizing must not charge the global in-flight bound per request.
+
+    `VllmConfig.max_in_flight_tokens` bounds scheduled-but-unsettled tokens
+    across ALL requests, so per-request pool sizing charges
+    `sliding_window - 1` plus the request's share of that global allowance.
+    The admission gate (`max_admission_blocks_per_request`) keeps the full
+    allowance so one large prefill is still admitted.
+    """
+    spec = new_sliding_window_spec(block_size=16, sliding_window=512)
+    max_in_flight = 32768
+    max_num_seqs = 16
+    config = SimpleNamespace(
+        parallel_config=SimpleNamespace(decode_context_parallel_size=1),
+        scheduler_config=SimpleNamespace(max_num_seqs=max_num_seqs),
+        model_config=SimpleNamespace(max_model_len=65536),
+        max_in_flight_tokens=max_in_flight,
+    )
+
+    amortized_tokens = 512 - 1 + max_in_flight // max_num_seqs
+    expected_blocks = amortized_tokens // 16 + (amortized_tokens % 16 > 0) + 1
+    assert spec.max_memory_usage_bytes(config) == (
+        expected_blocks * spec.page_size_bytes

+    # The admission gate still uses the full allowance.

+            max_in_flight_tokens=max_in_flight, max_model_len=65536
+        )

+    """Identify spec-decode drafter layers among `layer_names` by layer index.
+
+    EAGLE-family drafters (eagle/eagle3/mtp/dflash/dspark) register their
+    attention layers with indices continuing after the target model's layers,
+    so any layer whose index is >= the target's total layer count belongs to
+    the drafter. Returns an empty set when no such drafter is configured or
+    for layer names without a parseable index.

+    num_target_layers = vllm_config.model_config.get_total_num_hidden_layers()

I found a Qwen3.5 DFlash correctness case that appears to challenge the
assumption in commit 2 that SlidingWindowSpec is safe for DFlash draft layers.

Test setup:
- vLLM CPU v0.26.0, V2 model runner
- Target: Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound
- Draft: z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash retrain, revision
  30b0d54fe1e8aa5543387cc131503b2afe2f6a9c
- Draft layout: 5 sliding-attention layers and 1 full-attention layer
- 15 speculative tokens

Results:
| Configuration | Acceptance rate | Acceptance length |
|---|---:|---:|
| Original SlidingWindowSpec allocation | 2.29% | 1.34 |
| All-full-attention control | 33.03% | 5.95 |
| Hybrid compute with full KV allocation for SWA layers | 33.03% | 5.95 |
| Same fix without the causal=false override | 33.03% | 5.95 |

Setting the configured window to 262144, using only one sliding layer, and
using all sliding layers did not recover acceptance. The only change that
recovered it was retaining the layer's sliding-window compute configuration
while setting the inner Attention.sliding_window to None for KV-cache planning.

Qwen3 DFlash precomputes verifier-context K/V and writes it through absolute
context slot mappings. SlidingWindowManager's normal autoregressive block
recycling appears to invalidate that context.

I have a small Qwen3 patch matching Laguna's existing full-allocation behavior,
plus a focused regression test. Would you prefer this correctness case to be
handled in #50169 or in a separate PR? It may also be worth validating Laguna
acceptance quality, rather than coherence alone, before removing its safeguard.

Disclosure: GHC assisted the code/history investigation and patch
drafting. I reviewed the changes and ran the reported experiments.

Thanks for this, it found a real bug in the PR. You were right that the safety
argument in commit 2 was not established, and I have pushed a fix.

What I reproduced, on GB10 (CUDA), Laguna-S-2.1-NVFP4 + DFlash, V2 model runner,
15 speculative tokens, everything else held constant:

| Laguna config | draft acceptance | KV pool |
|---|---:|---:|
| windowed drafter, stock grouping | 0.29% (n=4, sd 0.08) | 871,430 |
| windowed drafter, drafter in its own KV group | 26.67% (n=2) | 871,430 |

Same pool either way, so this is not an allocation-size effect. The collapse
matches what you measured, and my earlier Laguna runs missed it because they
always had the grouping commit applied.

The root cause looks narrower than "SlidingWindowSpec is unsafe for DFlash". It
is a drafter layer sharing a KV cache group with target layers: the absolute
context slot mapping then resolves through the target's block table. Drafter
layers that have their groups to themselves are fine windowed. So the PR now
separates a drafter spec only when it would otherwise share a group, and the
window can stay.

On your model I could not reproduce the collapse on GPU. Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound
with z-lab/Qwen3.5-9B-DFlash at 30b0d54, V2 runner, 15 spec tokens:

| Qwen3.5 config | draft acceptance | KV pool |
|---|---:|---:|
| stock (windowed drafter) | 23.46% (n=5, sd 0.00) | 863,023 |
| full-attention drafter allocation | see note | 599,543 |
| this PR | 23.46% (n=5, sd 0.00) | 864,749 |

That model gives one KV group per layer, so its drafter never shares a group,
which is consistent with windowed being fine there. Stock and this PR produce
byte-identical spec-decode counters (accepted=813, drafted=3465 in every rep),
so the PR is exactly neutral on that model. The full-attention row is a
pool-only comparison; its acceptance was measured at a different generation
length and I have not re-run it like-for-like. Note that full allocation costs
31% of the pool there, which is why I would rather not apply it
unconditionally. Since your run was vLLM CPU v0.26.0, would you check whether
the CPU attention backend is the differentiating factor?

Your suggestion also caught a second bug. My first attempt separated the drafter
whenever its layers spanned several groups, which on Qwen3.5 merged five
single-layer groups into one five-layer group, violated the equal-layers-per-group
assumption in _get_kv_cache_groups_uniform_page_size, and cut its pool from 863k
to 185k. The pushed version keys on sharing rather than spanning, and I added a
regression test for the untouched case.

Happy to take the Qwen3 patch here if you still want the belt-and-braces
behaviour after the CPU/GPU question is settled, or to review it separately.



_Edited: replaced the Qwen3.5 acceptance figures, which had been taken at mismatched generation lengths, with like-for-like measurements._

Thanks for reproducing this and for updating the grouping logic. I’ll test stock current main on the same Xeon CPU with the original hybrid Qwen3.5 layout, then compare #50169 and full allocation on the same build if the collapse remains.

The prior CPU controls may be relevant: one sliding layer, all six sliding layers in one draft group, and a 262144-token window all remained near 2.3% acceptance. I’ll report the current-main version, KV grouping/pool logs, and like-for-like acceptance counters.

Follow-up: I tested the retrained Qwen3.5 DFlash checkpoint on a CPU nightly:

- vLLM: `0.26.1rc1.dev124+gb88916617`
- commit: `b88916617d3d2249bff0dae5cecb6b727c980a20`
- target: `Intel/Qwen3.5-9B-int4-AutoRound`

Result:

So current stock CPU nightly has healthy acceptance while retaining the checkpoint-declared sliding-window allocation. The recovery is already present before this PR; I have not isolated the exact intervening commit.

**Commit 3 can relax the startup feasibility gate below what runtime admission requires (hybrid MLA + sliding-window, large `max_model_len`)**

Thanks for this series — we carry commit 3 (`f401599bb`) downstream because without it our
config cannot start at all. Reporting a correctness concern about that commit specifically.

**Symptom.** The engine starts, logs a max-concurrency above 1.0 for `max_model_len`, and then
never schedules a single request of that size. The request sits in the waiting queue
indefinitely: `num_requests_waiting=1`, `num_requests_running=0`,
`iteration_tokens_total` stays at 0, `kv_cache_usage_perc` stays at 0. Cancelling the client
clears the queue and the server stays healthy. This is the #39734 deadlock shape.

**Why commit 3 is implicated.** `max_memory_usage_bytes` feeds
`_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` ("can we serve at least one request at `max_model_len`") and
`get_max_concurrency_for_kv_cache_config` (the logged concurrency). Commit 3 divides the
in-flight term by `max_num_seqs` there. The runtime path is unchanged and still charges the
full allowance: `allocate_slots(..., full_sequence_must_fit=scheduler_reserve_full_isl)`
(default `True`) computes the whole sequence via `get_num_blocks_to_allocate(...,
apply_admission_cap=True)` and compares against actual free blocks. So the startup gate can
pass at a pool the runtime gate will always reject.

**Config** (identical across all rows): vLLM v0.27.1 with only commit 3 applied;
DeepSeek-V4-Pro (MLA + two sliding-window sizes) + DSpark speculative decoding
(`num_speculative_tokens=7`); DP4 x EP4, prefill on 4x B300 (267.69 GiB each);
`max_model_len=1048576`, `max_num_seqs=64`, `max_num_batched_tokens=8192`,
`block_size=256`, fp8 KV, chunked prefill and prefix caching on, async scheduling on.

| `gpu_memory_utilization` | prefill KV pool | single 1,000,000-token request |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.94 | 9.60 GiB / 7,176 blocks | never scheduled (>12 min, zero iteration tokens) |
| 0.955 | 13.61 GiB / 10,179 blocks | never scheduled |
| 0.96 | 14.55 GiB / 10,880 blocks (DP0), 11,180 (DP1-3) | admitted, HTTP 200 in 176-187 s |

At 0.94 the startup log reads:

```text
GPU KV cache size: 1,780,544 tokens
Maximum concurrency for 1,048,576 tokens per request: 1.70x
```

Back-solving that line (`num_blocks / concurrency`) gives **4,226 blocks per `max_model_len`
request**, while the runtime gate demands **10,180-10,880 blocks** for a slightly smaller
(1,000,000-token) request — a **2.4-2.6x under-estimate**. The engine advertises 1.70x
concurrency for a request size it cannot admit even once.

A coarse bisect at 0.94 (7,176 blocks) puts the largest schedulable prompt between 300,000
and 400,000 tokens: 300k completes in 35 s, 400k is never scheduled.

**Supporting datapoint for the direction of the error.** Without commit 3, on the same model
and `max_model_len`, `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` demands 15.36 GiB and refuses to start
at 0.95 (12.27 GiB available). That is above the 13.6-14.55 GiB the runtime actually needs,
i.e. the un-amortized gate errs conservatively. The amortized gate crosses below it.

**We tested commit 1 (`ecb28b3fa`) on this config; it does not address this.** Rebased onto
v0.27.1 (4 of 5 hunks apply; the `same_type_layers` hunk needs a manual rebase because v0.27.1
inserts a "further merge same-type layers" step after that loop). Applicability checks passed
before running: `use_eagle()` covers `dspark`, and this model's DSpark drafter registers its
attention layers as `layers.{num_hidden_layers + i}`, so `_identify_drafter_layers` finds them.
With the commit applied, the startup accounting is unchanged — `Maximum concurrency` stays at
2.57x/2.65x and the DP0 pool at 10,873 vs 10,860 blocks — and the runtime behaviour is
unchanged too. The conditional separation appears not to trigger here, i.e. our drafter layers
already have their groups to themselves. No regression from it either.

**Operational consequence.** Because the gate passes, the operator ends up choosing
utilization from the wrong number, and the remaining device headroom has to absorb both
CUDA graph capture and execution scratch. With CUDA graphs enabled at the utilization that
admits 1M, graph capture takes 3.94 GiB/device and prefill then dies mid-request with
`torch.OutOfMemoryError: Tried to allocate 976.00 MiB ... 857-869 MiB is free`, killing the
engine core. Reproduced twice, with and without commit 1. Our current workaround is asymmetric:
CUDA graphs on the decode instance only, prefill forced eager. That restores throughput
(decode-side ITL P95 71 ms -> 15 ms on an internal agent benchmark) while keeping 1M
schedulable, but it is a workaround for the accounting gap, not a fix.

**Suggested direction.** If the amortized value is the right one for aggregate pool-capacity
planning, it may still be worth having `_check_enough_kv_cache_memory` — and ideally the
logged `Maximum concurrency` — use the same per-request bound the runtime admission gate uses
(`max_admission_blocks_per_request` with the full `max_in_flight_tokens`), so that "can one
`max_model_len` request fit" and "will the scheduler admit it" cannot disagree.

**What we did not establish.** We did not isolate which KV cache group's accounting produces
the 2.4x gap — only the aggregate. We have not written or tested a patch for the gap itself.
Happy to run any candidate on this config.

A data point relevant to commit 2 (keeping the drafter's checkpoint-declared window). It comes from a different model, but it is the same mechanism you'd get with a windowed Laguna drafter.

In #60560 we root-caused a DFlash2 acceptance drop (~40% → 27–29% at 32 concurrent sessions) that occurs only when the drafter's layers form a real sliding-window KV cache group. When `SlidingWindowManager` frees a block, the worker's block table keeps the old id. FA4 loads KV in 128-key tiles on SM100, so with 64-token pages the tile holding the window start can include one page that lies wholly outside the window. Once that freed block is reused, its bytes can decode as fp8 NaN, and masked NaN still reaches the attention output.

Two conditions hide it, so the GB10 checks here may not show it:
- **Low concurrency.** It nearly vanishes at concurrency 1 (37.9%), because freed blocks are rarely reused in time.
- **Tile size.** It needs the attention kernel's KV tile to be larger than the KV page. FA4 picks 64-key tiles on SM12x (for head dim > 64), so 64-token pages are safe there, while SM100 uses 128-key tiles.

It's worth re-checking Laguna acceptance on an SM100 GPU under sustained concurrency before relying on the windowed drafter. The fix, #60767 (nulling freed sliding-window entries in the worker's forward-pass block tables), would cover this PR's case too.
